subject: P11 dedicated authentication autocommit connection

reviewed_properties.finding: The private authentication handle is separate from every business root and does not issue BEGIN. Every existing auth SELECT and every principal/expiry/revocation check remains. No values, ACLs, resolved actors, or authority decisions are memoized.

Database identity derives from the already validated FileHandle stat before it closes. Each auth callback is fenced before/after by lstatSync regular-file/uid/private-mode/dev/ino and realpathSync equality. Missing/changed/unsafe paths fail closed and discard the old handle.
lifecycle.closed checked before callback and again before returning; inherited requireScope retains all ancestor closure/abort checks before and after the synchronous read.

db.inTransaction must be false before and after work; unexpected transaction or query error discards the reference before close and preserves the original rejection. Existing callbacks use Statement.get and return copies, with no retained iterator or asynchronous callback.

Existing refusal from a transaction scope and synchronous closed admission fence remain. Memoized disposal waits admitted active operations, then clears the dedicated handle and closes it once; materializations clear in finally even if close throws.
No changes to operation(write), queue ordering, active tracking, lock retries/timeouts, transactionAll, readSnapshotRoot, currentSnapshots, current authority, C08 namespaces, grants, or policies.

Only the createAuthenticationSecrets doc comment changes in the second file. Its statement now describes fresh committed autocommit reads and permits connection reuse without claiming a retained result/snapshot.

node:fs lstatSync/realpathSync are synchronous APIs; FileHandle.stat and lstatSync numeric dev/ino types match. Database type and inTransaction/close were already used in the same module. No new external dependency or API exposed.

qualification_needed: Real Bun/SQLite surgical control: warm store A auth reader, hold A canonical root, start store B revocation/removal and verify it remains pending, release the root, await B commit, then require a new auth read on the warmed A handle to observe that committed change.

Retain the existing Auth72 local pending-revocation/logout controls for immediate cancellation before durable write admission; do not confuse that fence with a peer commit during a held BEGIN IMMEDIATE root.
Physical replacement/unlink/symlink/permission changes after warmup must reject without returning prior credentials.
Closed/aborted scopes and disposal draining/idempotence must preserve denial and resource closure.
Installed five-case qualification remains required with original assertions/identities/budgets; static approval or component PASS cannot replace it.
performance_limit: D14 showed broad inclusive read/comparison latency and repeated operator authentication. This review establishes the concrete removed connection-open/PRAGMA/close amplification, but provides no isolated timings and does not predict how much wall time it saves.
residual_limits: Filesystem before/after identity checks do not claim atomic protection against arbitrary same-UID ABA replacement between syscalls; the existing path-opening mechanism has comparable external-race limits.
inTransaction detects explicit transaction contamination; callback discipline and surgical freshness tests must confirm no live statement/cursor retains an implicit snapshot.
New shared source content is an inert owner proposal/isolated candidate until authorized integration; no release or source-lease takeover is inferred.

documentary_correction.reason: Correct the proposed concurrency oracle to match the canonical BEGIN IMMEDIATE root; no product or postimage change.
documentary_correction.source: modules/sucafina/Sucafinav1/runtime/local-store.ts@d9eaac043514141abb2f1f978a6fd2ceaf4040d6: readSnapshotRoot invokes operation(true), which admits BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
documentary_correction.ordering: Warm store A authentication reader; A holds a canonical business/read root; store B starts revocation/removal and remains uncommitted while the lock is held; release A root; await B commit; A performs a new auth read using its warmed dedicated connection and observes the committed change.
documentary_correction.separate_inflight_fence: The existing Auth72 pending-revocation/logout fence covers immediate local cancellation before the durable write completes; it is distinct from visibility of another store commit.
documentary_correction.withdrawn_claim: A peer commits its auth write while the same LocalStore BEGIN IMMEDIATE business/read root remains held.
